resolvedIdentity: Rakkestad prestegård, gnr. 5/1, the protected rectory complex at Kirkeveien 116 beside Rakkestad church.

coordinateDecision.reason: The legacy point was near Rakkestad settlement. The applied point is the named Prestegard farm/rectory site and lies within metres of Lokalhistoriewiki's independent site coordinate.

sources.name: OpenStreetMap node 6259987033 – Prestegard
findings: Named farm/site point Prestegard at approximately 59.41279, 11.36889.
The point is south of the modern settlement and beside the church landscape.

sources.name: Lokalhistoriewiki – Rakkestad prestegård
findings: Coordinates 59.4127854, 11.3688136, within about five metres of the applied point.
The property is gnr. 5/1 at Kirkeveien 116 and lies about 150 metres from Rakkestad church.
The main building dates from 1797, was reduced from two storeys in 1838 and restored in 1922–1923.
Christian Frederik visited in 1814 and Crown Prince Karl Johan visited later.
The rectory tradition predates the Reformation and the complex contains several protected buildings.

sources.name: Allstad – Rakkestad prestebolig
findings: The log main building was erected in 1797 and altered in 1838.
The rectory also served as a post office for several decades.
The main building, storehouse and exteriors of later farm buildings are protected.
The complex underwent major rehabilitation in 2022–2023.
The property remains an active agricultural and residential estate.

sources.name: Riksantikvaren – Rakkestad prestegård decision
findings: The 2025 decision concerns alterations to the protected main building under the Cultural Heritage Act.
The facade and main-door setting remain subject to active heritage management.

sources.name: Nasjonalarkivet – Abdikasjonen
findings: Around 6,000 Norwegian troops were stationed in Rakkestad during the August 1814 campaign.
The military withdrawal from Rakkestad forms the wider context for the rectory's 1814 layer, but the source is not used to prove an exact meeting or visit inside the building.

rejectedCandidates.reason: Approximately 1.97 km north-west near the settlement and unsupported by a source-object contract.
Useful for main-building and visitor-address control, but less representative of the complete rectory complex and not a verified building footprint.
A separate medieval church building south of the rectory.
The landholding is much larger than the historic rectory yard and cannot be represented by the gameplay radius.

limits: The record does not claim that a formal cabinet meeting equivalent to Spydeberg occurred here.
The record does not claim that the Constitution or Convention of Moss was negotiated or signed here.
The military context in Rakkestad is wider than the rectory property.

accessAndSafety: The rectory is an active residential and agricultural property.
The coordinate does not grant access to the residence, yard, garden or farm buildings.
Gameplay should remain on lawful public roads or use explicit permission.
The 260-metre radius is not a building, heritage, property, garden, agricultural or access boundary.
